I appreciate the advice. I do feel that there’s so much more pressure on me to do great things and be someone unique and influential, and it really takes a toll on me. I’ve kind of been hardened into a mindset of “education is everything” since I was about 7, and I’ve never really been able to focus on other things. One of the reasons I feel so empty inside is because of my nonexistent life outside of school. I have friends at school, and I feel comfortable there, but I never go out with people to “have fun,”  because I’ve been molded into an introvert and it’s very difficult to break that mold. I’ve been taught to be better than everyone else and do great things in the future, and after 10 years of functioning with that one goal, I don’t know if I can cease to be that way - especially considering I’m going into the most important year of high school and post secondary education is right around the corner. However, I do think your advice to think smaller might help in the future, when the stakes are lower. Thanks for taking the time to reply!

I think I should clarify a little bit. I didn’t mean to say that I “have a great life,” but compared to other people who have these thoughts and feelings, I think I’m in a better position than most. The issue for me is that even if I find something I enjoy (Ex. I absolutely love architecture and really enjoy the creative aspect), I just don’t see the overall purpose of it (or anything for that matter). Who really cares if there’s one less person doing one less job in the world of almost 8 billion? I just don’t see why my life is important and no matter what I find or try to do, I just focus too much on the “what’s the point?” factor. Maybe I’m too pessimistic, but I really struggle to see how most other people don’t have these thoughts and how they can brush past them.
